dateline: Washington, D.C. / Baton Rouge, LA — January 2017–Present
heroHeadline: Cassidy Ousted in Louisiana Primary as MAGA Purge Claims Its Biggest Senate Scalp; SAVE Act Dead in Senate; Iran Ceasefire Day 78 — 20-Year Nuclear Offer Awaits Iranian Response
heroSubtitle: Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-LA) — one of seven Republicans who voted to convict Trump in the 2021 impeachment trial — was defeated in the May 16 Louisiana Republican primary (results confirmed May 17), finishing third as Trump-backed Rep. Julia Letlow led with ~45% and state Treasurer John Fleming advanced to a June 27 runoff with ~28%. Trump posted on Truth Social that Cassidy's political career is 'OVER!' — marking the first Senate primary defeat of a sitting Republican senator in nearly a decade and the most significant MAGA primary scalp to date. Separately, the SAVE America Act voter-ID bill — Trump's top election-security priority — effectively died in the Senate after Majority Leader Thune confirmed he would not revive the bill following its 48-50 procedural defeat, with Senators McConnell, Murkowski, Collins, and Tillis joining Democrats in opposition. On Iran (Day 78, May 17), Trump's 20-year nuclear enrichment suspension offer (announced May 15 on Air Force One) is awaiting a formal Iranian response; no new US-Iran direct talks are scheduled and the naval blockade of Iranian ports continues with ~41 tankers blocked. Trump's Beijing summit (May 14-15) produced no formal trade agreements despite his claims — Chinese officials publicly disputed his 'fantastic deals' characterization, and the planned $14 billion Taiwan arms sale remains uncertain as Trump called it a 'negotiating chip.'
